key_insight: A log‑barrier regularizer combined with a dual‑focused analysis yields an online algorithm for zero‑sum matrix games with bandit feedback that attains the optimal last‑iterate convergence rate matching the known t^{-1/4} lower bound (up to constants).
problem_solved: Closing the gap between lower bounds and achievable rates for last‑iterate convergence in uncoupled zero‑sum matrix games under bandit (partial) feedback — previous algorithms failed to reach the Omega(t^{-1/4)) barrier for exploitability.
method: Incorporate a log‑barrier regularizer into an online mirror descent framework to maintain interior iterates on the simplex and control geometry near the boundary.
Use bandit‑style gradient/feedback estimators (importance‑weighted sampling) adapted to the log‑barrier geometry to handle partial information.
Perform a dual‑focused theoretical analysis that directly bounds last‑iterate exploitability and shows the algorithm achieves the optimal t^{-1/4} convergence rate.
impact: Provides the first algorithmic recipe with matching optimal guarantees for last‑iterate convergence under limited feedback, improving reliability of practical minimax learning (e.g., adversarial training, GANs, multi‑agent RL) when only bandit feedback is available.
visual_elements: Line chart: exploitability vs iterations showing t^{-1/4} decay for the proposed method vs slower baselines
Schematic: zero‑sum matrix game loop with two uncoupled players, highlighting bandit feedback arrows and the log‑barrier update block
Diagram: simplex geometry illustrating how the log‑barrier keeps iterates interior and avoids boundary instability
Flowchart: algorithm steps (sample, estimate bandit feedback, log‑barrier mirror update, repeat) with a badge showing 'optimal rate'
paper_title: Optimal last-iterate convergence in matrix games with bandit feedback using the log-barrier
paper_authors: Come Fiegel, Pierre Menard, Tadashi Kozuno, Michal Valko, Vianney Perchet
